gaps.note: The datasheet (v1) Management Interfaces row lists one rear CPU/BMC shared Ethernet RJ45 beside the serial console and the USB port, and gives it no rate; no other staged document describes the rear panel.
gaps.wanted: the rate of the rear CPU/BMC shared Ethernet jack (10/100/1000 or otherwise), so the port can state a `speed`.

gaps.note: The supplies are very probably Gospower G1251-0550WN-series 550 W CRPS modules taking AC or high-voltage DC through one inlet - a visual match on every feature against that module's photographs (see maiaedge/psu-550w@1's `identity`), and the Port Extender datasheet's "100-240VAC or 180-300VDC" is that module's range. But no document names the part, so its model is not recorded and no -48 V DC option is modelled or known.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of one supply's rating label - it is on the module's body, so pull one supply to take it.

gaps.note: EVERY REAR POSITION IS ESTIMATED, and the left half is inferred. The setup video shows the right half obliquely and never the left; the order drawn - supply, two fans, management panel, two fans, supply - is the right half observed and mirrored, which the datasheet's inventory (two supplies, four fans) and the documentation's "center of the device" management jack both support but do not prove. The fan module's size, the supplies' faces and the USB port's place on the panel are all unmeasured. Tracked with the maintainer's pending photographs.
gaps.wanted: a face-on photograph of the rear, or a mechanical drawing of it.

gaps.note: These faces draw the envelope, in the bare steel the video shows, and nothing on it. The envelope is dimensioned - 44 x 438 x 520 on page 3 of the datasheet. The video shows what is on the lid - two recessed finger pulls, a product label near the middle and a yellow warning sticker at the rear right corner - but only obliquely, so none of them is placed.
gaps.wanted: square-on photographs of the lid, the underside and a flank.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (rear 6); `physical-context` on port group ports - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis-finish.note: the MaiaEdge setup video (Step 5, "Attach Side Rails to the Port Extender", on the vendor's YouTube channel) and the maintainer's stills of it: the lid, flanks and rear are BARE GALVANISED STEEL, and only the front face is black. The first model drew the whole box black.

front-vents.note: rectangular slots along both edges: the top row from x 32.6 (past the wordmark) to 428, 3.9 x 2.0 mm on a 5.02 pitch; the bottom from 5.4 to 432, 2.9 x 1.7 on about 4.0, interrupted by screws. `slots-h` draws its slot at a fixed 9/14 of its tile, so the slots are drawn somewhat narrower than they are; the pitch and the row are right.

lamps.note: read off the page-1 render, and it settles what the first model's `tenant-port-lamps` gap could not: the round features above and below the SFP rows are LAMPS, one per port - dark 2.45 mm lenses with no screw slot, at y 6.96 above each top-row port and 35.76 below each bottom-row one, centred on the column. Each uplink has FOUR in a row on a 4.05 mm pitch, centred on the port, at y 6.45 and 36.1 - not the two-and-two band common/qsfp28-cage@3 draws, which is why that part is no longer fitted (maiaedge/port-extender-lane-leds@1 is). What any lamp means is not stated.

logo.note: the MaiaEdge mark sits at x 2.9 to 8.3, y 1.4 to 7.0, and IS NOT DRAWN - vendor logos are not reproduced (library/components/README.md). The wordmark beside it is set as text, white, x 9.7 to 25.9 with its capitals 3.2 mm tall.

numbering.note: read off the page-1 render: every column is printed "N (up)(down) N+1" on one line between the rows - odd port above, even below, 1 to 56 - with the two numerals hugging a pair of arrows. That is the column-major numbering the first model derived, now read rather than derived, and it agrees with every port number the product documentation names (41-44 and 48 among the tenants; 51-56 among the uplinks, a PBC cabled to 51 and 52). Digits 1.54 mm tall, baseline y 22.23; arrows 1.5 mm each, 0.44 apart, drawn centred on their column - the render puts them 0.1 to 0.3 mm left of it, which is inside what it can resolve.

port-ids.note: EVERY PORT IS `port-N`, INCLUDING THE EIGHT UPLINKS, and that is not cosmetic. dcim_export treats a placement as an interface only when its id starts with `port-`; the first draft called the uplinks `uplink-49`..`uplink-56` and the NetBox and Nautobot exports came out with 48 interfaces instead of 56, silently. The uplink's ROLE is carried by the part it is placed from (common/qsfp28-cage@3, media qsfp28) and by `numbering` below, which is where a role belongs - the id carries the number the vendor addresses it by.

ports.note: datasheet page 3 - "Tenant Ports: 48 x SFP28 10GbE / 25GbE" and "Fabric Uplink Ports: 8 x QSFP28 100GbE". 48 + 8 = 56, WHICH RECONCILES THE TWO PORT COUNTS IN CIRCULATION: the marketing copy says "48 ports" and the product documentation calls it "a 56-port switch", and both are right.

positions.note: read off the page-1 render. SFP28: three blocks of eight columns by two rows starting at x 5.04, 122.05 and 239.07 on the SFF-8433 14.25 mm pitch, 3.0 mm between blocks; rows at y 9.62 and 23.35 (13.73 apart - the first model had 16.4). QSFP28: one block of four columns by two rows at x 356.45 on the 19.0 mm ganged pitch, rows at 10.21 and 24.03. THE LAMPS SET THE PITCH, NOT THE CAGES: the cage outlines read 14.33 mm apart and the lamps on the face beside them 14.25, because the cages stand proud of the face and the render's perspective magnifies them about 0.56% more. Corrected for that, every cage centre lands on its lamp.

power.note: datasheet page 3 - "1+1 Redundant, Hot-Swappable PSUs (100-240VAC or 180-300VDC auto-ranging)" and "< 500W Maximum (Typical < 350W at 25C)".

rear.note: ORDER OBSERVED, POSITIONS ESTIMATED. The video shows only the right half of the rear, and only obliquely at 640 x 360: from the right end, a CRPS supply (a 550W label, a C14 inlet with a cord clip), two fan modules (black, honeycomb grille, blue pull handle, red tab), and a small panel with two RJ45 jacks stacked one above the other; a third fan starts past it. The datasheet completes the inventory - "1+1 Redundant, Hot-Swappable PSUs", "3+1 Redundant Fans", and "1 x Rear CPU/BMC Shared Ethernet (RJ45) - 1 x Serial Console (RJ45) - 1 x USB Type-A" - and the product documentation puts the management jack "on the rear ... center of the device, at the top". So the rear is drawn SYMMETRIC: a supply at each end, two fans either side, and the management panel in the middle with the Ethernet jack on top. Every coordinate is chosen to fit that inventory into 438 mm with the small gaps the stills show. The supply is maiaedge/psu-550w@1, the PBC-2000's: the video shows the same face - 550W label, C14 with a cord clip - and the datasheet's input range is that part's.

size.note: datasheet - MaiaEdge-Port-Extender-Datasheet-v1.pdf page 3, "Dimensions (H x W x D) 44 mm x 438 mm x 520 mm (1U EIA Rackmount)". NOT the PBC-2000's envelope: that box is 41.27 x 437.90 x 291.08, so this one is taller and 229 mm deeper, and nothing may be borrowed between them.

source-render.note: THE FRONT IS MEASURED OFF THE DATASHEET'S OWN RENDER, which the first model never used. MaiaEdge-Port-Extender-Datasheet-v1.pdf embeds a 6000 x 3373 image on page 1 (`pdfimages -list` finds it; the staged 800 px marketing render is a different, angled asset), and it is square to the face: scaled on the datasheet's 438 mm across (x 610 to 5552 px, 11.28 px/mm) it reads the face 43.2 mm tall against 44 - 1.8%, the lid showing above. Measured per axis: 11.28 px/mm across, 11.07 down. Staged as working/intake/maiaedge/port-extender/renders/datasheet-p1-front-render-6000.png.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 24 SFP pairs (port-1/port-2 to port-47/port-48), the 4 QSFP pairs (port-49/port-50 to port-55/port-56). 24 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward.

thermal.note: datasheet page 3 - "3+1 Redundant Fans; Front-to-Back and Back-to-Front configurations available". BOTH directions are offered, so no airflow is asserted: the same hole is an intake on one SKU and an exhaust on another.
